# Backend Patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor: a dense reference of backend architecture patterns for building or reviewing Node.js, Express, and Next.js API routes and their data access. Covers resource-based REST URL design with filtering, sorting, and pagination conventions, the repository pattern for abstracting data access (with a worked Supabase example), the service layer for keeping business logic out of controllers, database optimization (N+1 queries, indexing, connection pooling), and caching strategies across Redis, in-memory stores, and HTTP cache headers. Also touches background jobs and async processing, structured error handling and validation, and middleware for auth, logging, and rate limiting. Written as pass/fail code examples, so an agent can apply the patterns directly while writing or reviewing code. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: Node.js and TypeScript oriented throughout; the ideas transfer to other stacks but the examples will not compile elsewhere. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
